key_findings: Inspected the scaffold (CADS-webconference-android@4ea9b88) and CADS-Tunnel's crates: MainActivity is a placeholder TextView, matching the flagship goal (a real Agent-Fabric channel-join + Noise_IK handshake + WebRTC client, matching ct-agent-wasm's browser behavior). Checked what's actually reusable: the Noise_IK handshake (crates/client/src/noise.rs) and the Agent-Fabric channel/service primitives (crates/common) are pure Rust; crates/common only exposes a wasm-bindgen ('js' feature) path for browsers today (see Cargo.toml comment: 'wasm-bindgen, not a syscall'). ct-agent itself lives in its own repo (scimbe/ct-agent). There is no existing Android/JNI path anywhere in this ecosystem. Reimplementing Noise_IK and channel-session logic natively in Kotlin would duplicate and risk diverging from the already-audited Rust implementation used by every other client (ct-agent, ct-client, the wasm browser path) -- a real correctness/security risk, not a style preference.
constraints: devsystem.android_native_bridge: The Android client needs Agent-Fabric channel-join + Noise_IK, both already implemented in Rust (crates/client/src/noise.rs, crates/common). Proposing a new stage/service: build a JNI bridge (cargo-ndk or UniFFI) that compiles ct-client's/ct-common's existing Rust crypto+session code for android-arm64/x86_64 and exposes it to Kotlin directly, instead of reimplementing Noise_IK by hand in Kotlin. This mirrors the existing wasm-bindgen browser path (same Rust core, different target) rather than inventing a second, divergent implementation. This is an architecture-defining decision (which library/toolchain, how the JNI surface is shaped) with real security stakes (Noise_IK handshake correctness) -- it should get a human check-in before implementation work starts, not proceed unsupervised.

key_findings: The check-in delivered on iteration 5 (mandatory checkin_every cadence) blocked the run pending a real human decision on devsystem.android_native_bridge: cargo-ndk vs UniFFI for the Rust->Android bridge. The operator answered directly (not via the pipeline's own channels this time, but in the driving conversation): UniFFI-generated bindings, not hand-written JNI -- matching the research doc's own lean (docs/android-native-bridge-options.md), citing UniFFI's real async support (matches ct-client's actual tokio/quinn-based async flow) and reduced hand-written FFI surface area for the code that will eventually handle key material/handshake state. cargo-ndk is still needed regardless, for cross-compilation. Plan for this iteration and the next: a minimal, honest spike first -- a trivial UniFFI-exported Rust function, cross-compiled via cargo-ndk, Kotlin bindings generated, wired into the Gradle build and called from MainActivity -- proving the toolchain works end to end in this actual environment BEFORE touching the real Noise_IK/Agent-Fabric code. Real-device/emulator execution can't be verified on this resource-constrained host (no working Android emulator available); build-time verification (assembleDebug packaging the .so + generated Kotlin compiling) is the honest scope for this slice.

Wired the toolchain-spike artifacts from iteration 6 (UniFFI-generated native_bridge.kt, cross-compiled libnative_bridge.so for arm64-v8a/x86_64) into the actual Gradle build and MainActivity, closing out devsystem.android_native_bridge's Gradle-integration slice. Added net.java.dev.jna:jna:5.17.0@aar to app/build.gradle.kts -- verified as the only dependency needed by reading native_bridge.kt's imports directly (only com.sun.jna.*), not by guessing; the @aar classifier requirement and minimum version were cross-checked against UniFFI's own Kotlin Gradle guide. Deliberately did NOT add kotlinx-coroutines-core: the generated file's 'Async support' section is an empty comment header, since bridge_version() isn't an async UniFFI export -- adding an unused dependency would have been guessing, not verifying. MainActivity now calls the real uniffi.native_bridge.bridgeVersion() (a genuine JNA FFI call into libnative_bridge.so) and renders its return value, wrapped in a catch(e: LinkageError) fallback. That fallback isn't speculative defensive coding -- the first hermetic test run actually failed with UnsatisfiedLinkError, because libnative_bridge.so is cross-compiled by cargo-ndk against Android's Bionic libc and cannot load under Robolectric's host-JVM/glibc test environment; the fallback and an updated MainActivityTest make that a real, exercised code path instead of a build break. Verified hermetically via mingc/android-build-box (this run's established pattern): ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest assembleDebug --no-daemon --stacktrace -> BUILD SUCCESSFUL, 1 test / 0 failures. Verified both ABI .so files are actually packaged inside app-debug.apk (not just present on disk) via a zipfile listing: lib/arm64-v8a/libnative_bridge.so and lib/x86_64/libnative_bridge.so, both present with real non-zero sizes. Pushed to CADS-webconference-android@f406927 (aa8696d..f406927). NOT verified and not claimed: real on-device/emulator execution -- this host has no working Android emulator, so nothing here proves the app actually displays the real bridge_version() string when launched. What was verified is that the code builds, both ABI native libs ship inside the APK, and the LinkageError fallback path is real and exercised (proving the FFI call is genuinely wired, not stubbed) -- the success-path render on a real device remains unverified pending real-device access.
constraints: devsystem.android_native_build_ci: Discovered while doing this iteration's work, not speculatively: native-bridge/build-android.sh's own header comment states the .so/.kt artifacts it produces 'are committed for now (this is still the toolchain spike, not yet CI-integrated -- see the #382 run notes for the follow-up to build these from source in CI instead)'. Right now app/src/main/jniLibs/*/libnative_bridge.so and app/src/main/java/uniffi/native_bridge/native_bridge.kt are manually generated on a developer/agent host and committed as opaque binary + generated-source artifacts -- CI (devsystem.verify's GitHub Actions run) only ever compiles the Kotlin/Gradle side and never rebuilds them from native-bridge/src/lib.rs. For a toolchain spike with a trivial bridge_version() function this is a low-stakes gap, but it will not remain low-stakes: this same path is slated to carry the real Noise_IK/Agent-Fabric crypto code (per #382's plan), at which point an unreproducible, manually-regenerated .so sitting in git history becomes a real supply-chain and correctness concern (no CI proof the committed binary matches the committed Rust source). Proposing a stage that runs native-bridge/build-android.sh (or an equivalent cargo-ndk + uniffi-bindgen invocation) inside CI and either verifies the committed artifacts are reproducible or replaces committing them at all in favor of a CI-produced build output.
